newsitem.title: UK: UK current account surplus rises in Q1.
newsitem.headline: UK current account surplus rises in Q1.

text.p: Britain recorded a 1.459 billion pound seasonally adjusted surplus on its balance of payments current account in the first quarter of this year, figures published on Friday showed.
This compared with a 508 million pound surplus in the fourth quarter of 1996 and a deficit of 1.21 billion pounds in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The surplus was well above market expectations of around 500 million pounds.
Other figures showed that the British economy grew by 3.1 percent year on year in the first quarter, an upward revision of initial projections of 3.0 percent growth.

In a further sign of a buoyant economy, the British Bankers' Association said net lending to house buyers by the major was a seasonally adjusted 803 million pounds in May, the highest figure since January.
